explanation: OEIS A157225 (number of ways to write the n-th odd number 2n−1 as p + 2^x + 7·2^y, p prime ≡ 5 mod 6, x, y ≥ 1): Z.-W. Sun conjectured a(n) = 0 iff n < 11 or n ∈ {13, 16, 992}, and the entry records a disproof with n = 716993899. The formal a counts the representations (x, y ≤ 2n−1 suffices), and the statement negates Sun's characterisation for n > 0. I verified the counterexample: 2·716993899 − 1 = 1433987797 has no such representation (checked all x, y < 40, which covers every 2^x + 7·2^y below it). Faithful.
